title: Prerequisites for Learning NumPy
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of prerequisites for learning numpy and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply python variables and data types to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for prerequisites for learning numpy.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 7 of the supplied curriculum: **Prerequisites for Learning NumPy**. The main starting point is **Python variables and data types**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Clear mental models prevent learners from treating NumPy as just another syntax layer. It is a library for numerical arrays and array-oriented operations; it is not a replacement for every Python data structure or every scientific library.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Prerequisites for Learning NumPy** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Python variables and data types** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an ndarray exactly like a Python list
common_mistakes.why: Some list operations concatenate sequences while array operations are numeric and element-wise.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the type and dtype, then write the intended element-wise expression explicitly.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming NumPy is always the best tool
common_mistakes.why: Specialized data frames, sparse arrays, or domain libraries may fit a task better.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose NumPy for dense array-oriented numerical work and use other tools when the data model calls for them.
